summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Watson & Crick (1953) B-DNA model: right-handed, antiparallel double helix (2.0 nm diameter, 3.4 nm pitch, 10 bp/turn, 0.34 nm axial rise). A=T (2 H-bonds) and G≡C (3 H-bonds). Eukaryotic chromatin packaging: 2 m DNA packaged into 6 μm nucleus via nucleosome core octamer (147 bp DNA wrapped 1.65 turns), H1 linker (chromatosome 167 bp), 30 nm solenoid fiber, and metaphase scaffold (1400 nm).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
B-DNA DOUBLE HELIX PARAMETERS
                         
   Strand Directionality    ──► Antiparallel strands (5' -> 3' and 3' -> 5')
   Helical Handedness       ──► Right-handed double helix
   Helical Diameter         ──► 2.0 nm (20 Å)
   Helical Pitch (One Turn) ──► 3.4 nm (34 Å)
   Base Pairs per Turn      ──► 10 base pairs (bp) per turn
   Axial Rise per Base Pair ──► 0.34 nm (3.4 Å) between adjacent pairs
   Base Pairing Hydrogen    ──► A = T (2 Hydrogen Bonds);
   Bond Architecture            G = C (3 Hydrogen Bonds)
conceptBreakdown.content:
### 3.1 B-DNA Structural Parameters (Watson & Crick, 1953)
- **Antiparallel Strands**: One strand runs $5' \rightarrow 3'$, and the complementary strand runs $3' \rightarrow 5'$.
- **Right-Handed Helix**: Displays a major groove ($2.2\text{ nm}$) and a minor groove ($1.2\text{ nm}$).
- **Helical Dimensions**: Diameter = $2.0\text{ nm}$ ($20\text{ \AA}$), Pitch = $3.4\text{ nm}$ ($34\text{ \AA}$), Base pairs per turn = $10\text{ bp}$, Axial rise = $0.34\text{ nm}$ ($3.4\text{ \AA}$). Base pairs stack perpendicularly like steps of a spiral staircase.

### 3.2 Chromatin Packaging Hierarchy in Eukaryotes
- In human diploid cells, **$2\text{ meters}$ of DNA** ($\approx 6.6 \times 10^9\text{ bp}$) is packaged into a nucleus of **$6\ \mu\text{m}$ diameter**.

```
                        NUCLEOSOME CORE PARTICLE ARCHITECTURE
                        
    Octameric Histone Core ──► [(H2A-H2B)₂ + (H3-H4)₂]
    Wrapped DNA Length     ──► 147 base pairs (bp) in 1.65 left-handed superhelical turns
    Linker DNA             ──► 20--80 bp bound to Histone H1 (= Chromatosome 167 bp)
```

```
                        EUKARYOTIC CHROMATIN PACKAGING
                        
   Naked DNA (2 nm) ──► 10 nm "Beads-on-a-String" Nucleosomes
                                      │
   Chromasome Solenoid Fiber (30 nm) ◄── Stabilized by Histone H1
                                      │
   Scaffolded Chromatin Loops (300 nm) ──► Metaphase Chromosome (1400 nm)
```

conceptBreakdown.heading: Euchromatin vs. Heterochromatin
conceptBreakdown.title: Euchromatin vs. Heterochromatin
conceptBreakdown.content: Euchromatin is loosely packed, lightly staining 10 nm fiber with active gene transcription; Heterochromatin (constitutive and facultative) is densely packed, darkly staining 30-100 nm fiber that is transcriptionally silent.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Histone Post-Translational Modifications
conceptBreakdown.title: Histone Post-Translational Modifications
conceptBreakdown.content: Histone tails undergo post-translational modifications (acetylation by HATs neutralizes positive lysine charge, opening chromatin for transcription; methylation by HMTs can activate or repress gene expression).
